ops.title: v0.22: publish cdhash beside sha256; decide prefers cdhash-vs-cdhash
ops.description: The raceless identity exists: csops CS_OPS_CDHASH on self returns the cdhash of the image the kernel validated at exec. internal/trust already reads it for peers (verify.go:17 opCDHash, :134) and parses signature superblobs to match a CodeDirectory to a cdhash (blob.go:123-135) — the machinery a launcher-side static "cdhash of this file" needs. darwin/arm64 Go binaries are ad-hoc signed by the linker and bundled apps are Developer ID signed, so every fleet binary carries a cdhash. The fix is not small because build identity is record-schema-visible: switching daemon-published identity desynchronizes it from Program.build() and every v0.21 record on disk, so the record carries both digests for one release cycle (the same one-cycle pattern as the bbolt sweep). GATE: fleet on v0.21 in production plus one observed upgrade cycle. Decision record: the 2026-08-02 owner decision chose defer-and-document; the serve.go TODO was rewritten as a documented residual naming this task's shape.

ops.text: Serve publishes a CS_OPS_CDHASH self-read (beside internal/trust's peer path) in the owner record alongside sha256, for one release cycle
Program.build()/decide prefer cdhash-vs-cdhash when both sides carry one; the static side derives cdhash from the file via internal/trust's CodeDirectory parsing (blob.go:123-135)
The bundled dual-read residual documented at serve.go buildDigest and program.go:218-227 is closed: a test proves a replaced bundle executable is detected as divergence, and both comments retire
scripts/test.sh -race -count=1 ./... green; mixed-era green both directions
